seo.title: Spice Coast Cruises Alleppey: Luxury Houseboat Review
seo.description: Spice Coast Cruises Kerala backwater honeymoon review. Private teak kettuvallam, full crew, all meals. Score 84/100, from $450/night.

content.verdict: Spice Coast Cruises is the CGH Earth operation that took the standard Alleppey houseboat and quietly made it serious — solar-powered, single-cabin private kettuvallams hand-built from old teak and bamboo with coir-rope binding, a three-person crew (captain, engineer, chef), and a route that deliberately avoids the busy main lake in favour of small canals where village life still happens at the water\'s edge. For 24 hours your floor-to-ceiling air-conditioned cabin opens onto an open lounge deck with rattan armchairs, and meals are cooked in front of you on the back-deck stove from ingredients picked up that morning at a village market. It is the single best honeymoon night in Kerala, full stop — though 1 night is the right dose, not 2. A typical itinerary boards at 12pm, lunches in motion, anchors at a small village for sunset (you can step ashore to watch the fishermen), serves a kingsize-spice Kerala dinner under the stars on the deck, sleeps on the lake, and wakes you with masala chai at the bedroom door before disembarking at 9am the next day. Pair it with land-based nights at Niraamaya or Kumarakom Lake Resort either side so you have a proper hotel for showers, swimming and decompressing — the boat is the highlight, not the entire backwater stay.
content.best_room: There is only one cabin per boat — that is the point. You and the crew, nobody else. The Premium Pamba kettuvallam (slightly larger, with a separate reading lounge) is the upgrade worth taking on a honeymoon.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Arrival Cochin, transfer to Alleppey
itinerary_7_nights.description: From COK airport drive 90 minutes to Alleppey. Overnight at a transit hotel (Lemon Tree Alleppey or Punnamada Resort) to reset and acclimate. Light dinner, early bed.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Board the kettuvallam
itinerary_7_nights.description: 12pm boarding at the private Spice Coast jetty. Welcome coconut, route briefing, and the boat slips into the canals. Lunch of karimeen pollichathu on the open deck. Slow afternoon, dawn-village anchor for sunset and shore walk.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Dawn coffee, disembark, drive to Munnar
itinerary_7_nights.description: Wake at 6am to masala chai delivered to the cabin door. Slow breakfast on the deck as the boat returns to the jetty. Disembark 9am. 5-hour drive up into the Munnar tea hills, check-in at Windermere Estate.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Munnar plantation day
itinerary_7_nights.description: Tea estate walk with a planter, factory tour, picnic lunch at the highest viewpoint, sunset at the Mattupetty dam. Dinner on the bungalow veranda.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Drive down to Marari Beach
itinerary_7_nights.description: 5-hour drive via Thekkady. Arrive Marari Beach Resort. Hammock afternoon, sunset on the beach watching the chemmeen-vala nets pulled in.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Marari beach day, Ayurveda
itinerary_7_nights.description: Long beach morning. Couples 90-minute Abhyanga. Lunch of fresh-caught fish. Sunset cocktail at the beach bar.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Final morning, drive to Cochin
itinerary_7_nights.description: Slow breakfast, swim. Drive 90 minutes back to Cochin. One last night at Brunton Boatyard or direct to COK for the evening flight home.

caveats: Mosquitos at dusk are real — use the supplied repellent and keep the cabin doors closed at sunset.
The boat does not move at night — moored from sunset to dawn, by law.
Wifi is patchy; treat the night as a digital detox.

faqs.question: How is Spice Coast different from a standard Alleppey houseboat?
faqs.answer: Solar-powered, only 4 boats in the fleet (vs 1,400 commercial houseboats), routed through small canals rather than the busy main lake, and a CGH Earth operation with proper kitchen standards.

faqs.question: 1 night or 2?
faqs.answer: 1 night is perfect. By the second day the romance fades into wanting a real shower. Combine with land-based stays at Niraamaya or Kumarakom Lake Resort.

faqs.question: Are meals included?
faqs.answer: Yes — all meals, snacks, masala chai, soft drinks, and the welcome coconut. Alcohol is BYO; the boat will chill your wine.

faqs.question: Is the bathroom proper?
faqs.answer: Yes — full ensuite with rainfall shower, sink, and toilet. Hot water available on demand from the solar system.

faqs.question: How private is the route?
faqs.answer: Highly — small canals, village banks, very few other tourist boats. The main lake (Vembanad) is avoided entirely.

faqs.question: When is the best time?
faqs.answer: November through March. June–September the canals can be flooded by monsoon and routes restricted.
